newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-Mar 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-Mar 12.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa pledged not to undermine the present government after announcing the transfer of two key officials to his post-handover administration.
-- The World Bank said China needed to take decisive steps to direct more of its foreign investment towards its poorer interior and redress the growing imbalance between the regions.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Financial Secretary Donald Tsang will underscore continuity and prudence in his budget, which could project a surplus of up to HK$40 billion for 1997/98.
-- SING TAO -- Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa said his office would not become a second power centre before the handover and that his team would cooperate with the colonial government.
-- MING PAO -- A Chinese official in charge of relations with Taiwan said the Taiwanese journalist who hijacked a flight to the mainland had not asked for political asylum.
-- WEN WEI PO -- A Chinese official said repatriation of the Taiwanese hijacker had been complicated by the fact that Taipei had refused to send Chinese hijackers back to the mainland.

--TA KUNG PAO -- A Chinese official said China would make it convenient for Taiwanese to come to Hong Kong after the handover. He said an announcement would be made in a few months' time over regulations on necessary travel documents.
-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- The second-hand property market boomed in March, with speculators focusing on housing estates in the New Territories.
